records.question: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
search_queries: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
records.answer:
F-1 students (and their dependents) currently have a **60-day grace period** after their program ends, according to the [ISSS page on maintaining status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain).

**During the grace period you may:**
- Prepare to leave the U.S.
- Travel within the U.S.

You may **not** work or study. If you aren't applying for OPT or extending your status, you're expected to depart during this period. If you leave before it ends, you can't re-enter in F-1 status after your I-20 expiration date.

**Related points:**
- If you apply for post-completion OPT, USCIS must receive your application before the 60 days end. Your F-1 status then stays active while the application is pending ([OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)).
- A 60-day grace period also follows the end of post-completion OPT or STEM OPT, but only if you completed it. It doesn't apply if you exceeded the unemployment limit (90 days for OPT, 150 days for STEM OPT).

**Proposed change:** On September 16, 2025, ISSS posted about a *proposed* DHS rule that would reduce the F-1 grace period to 30 days and replace duration of status with fixed periods of stay ([announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/September/DHS-Proposes-to-Replace-Duration-of-Status-for-F-and-J-Visa-Holders-with-Fixed-Periods-of-Stay)). I didn't find a final rule in the excerpts, so the 60 days is what the ISSS pages currently state. Please confirm with an ISSS advisor for your own situation.

records.question: Is the new rule ending duration of status in effect now?
search_queries: Is the new rule ending duration of status in effect now?
records.answer:
No. According to ISSS, the rule is not currently in effect.

- **Final rule (posted July 17, 2026):** DHS [published a final rule eliminating duration of status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/July/Department-of-Homeland-Security-Publishes-Final-Rule-Eliminating-Duration-of-Status) for F and J nonimmigrants. It was scheduled to take effect on September 15, 2026.
- **Court order (posted September 14, 2026):** The U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts issued a preliminary injunction. Under that order, the rule [will no longer go into effect on September 15, and DHS is barred from implementing it](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status).

ISSS says it is monitoring guidance from DHS, ICE, USCIS, and the Department of State, and will update its guidance as more information becomes available. The excerpts I have don't show any update after the September 14 post, so I can't say what happens next.

If you're planning travel or need an I-20 extension, confirm your situation with an ISSS advisor. ISSS also has an FAQ page on the final rule in the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/Final-Rule-Eliminating-Duration-of-Status-(D-S)---FAQs.aspx).

records.question: Which countries are affected by the travel ban proclamation?
search_queries: Which countries are affected by the travel ban proclamation?
records.answer:
The most recent ISSS list comes from the expanded proclamation, which was signed December 16, 2025 and took effect January 1, 2026. It covers 38 countries plus the Palestinian territories. ISSS lists the countries as:

Afghanistan, Angola, Antigua and Barbuda, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burma, Burundi, Chad, Republic of Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Cuba, Dominica, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Gabon, The Gambia, Haiti, Iran, Laos, Libya, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Tanzania, Togo, Tonga, Turkmenistan, Venezuela, Yemen, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Travelers using Palestinian Authority-issued or -endorsed travel documents are also subject to the ban. This list comes from [ISSS's January 2026 post](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/January/USCIS-issues-a-policy-memorandum-that-places-a-hold-on-all-pending-applications-for-individuals-from).

- **Visas:** [The December 2025 expansion](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/December/presidential-proclamation-expansion-restricting-entry-us) says F and J visas are suspended for both fully and partially restricted countries. It also says the partial ban on Turkmenistan was lifted.
- **Earlier version:** The [June 2025 proclamation](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/June/Presidential-proclamation-establishes-travel-bans-on-19-countries) covered 19 countries and has been expanded by the December proclamation.
- **Travel advice:** If you are a national of one of these countries, [ISSS advises](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/March/International-Travel-Advisory---Spring-2026) that you should not leave the U.S. without consulting ISSS first, whether or not you have a valid visa.

Exceptions and details can change. To check how this applies to you, contact ISSS at isss@drexel.edu.

records.question: Can I still take most of my classes online like students did during COVID?
search_queries: Can I still take most of my classes online like students did during COVID?
records.answer:
No. The COVID-era flexibilities ended, and the current rule is that F-1 and J-1 students can count no more than 3 credits of online or distance coursework toward full-time enrollment each term. That means undergraduates need at least 9 credits, and graduate students at least 6 credits, in face-to-face or hybrid classes each term ([Maintaining F-1 and J-1 Student Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain)).

Some related details from ISSS's [June 2, 2023 announcement on the termination of SEVP COVID-19 flexibilities](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2023/June/termination-of-sevp-covid-19-flexibilities):
- Hybrid classes count as in-person classes for immigration purposes.
- Starting fall 2023, ISSS can't keep a SEVIS record active for students studying online from outside the U.S. To stay active, you must be in the U.S., live within commuting distance of campus, and enroll in in-person or hybrid courses.
- International students can't enroll in programs that are fully or mainly online.

There is one exception to the full-time requirement. Students in their final term may be able to apply for less than full time, but they still can't take courses fully online in that term ([Less Than Full Time](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/less-than-full-time)).

If your course plan includes online classes, confirm it with an ISSS advisor before you register.

records.question: Do I need to show proof of COVID vaccination to fly back to the U.S.?
search_queries: Do I need to show proof of COVID vaccination to fly back to the U.S.?
records.answer:
No. According to ISSS, the [COVID vaccination requirement for non-immigrants traveling to the U.S. ended at the end of the day on May 11, 2023](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2023/May/end-of-covid-vaccination-requirement), when the COVID-19 public health emergency officially ended (post dated May 9, 2023).

Older ISSS announcements about vaccination and testing, such as the [November 2021 vaccination requirement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2021/October/new-policy-to-require-foreign-nationals-traveling-to-the-us-to-be-fully-vaccinated) and the [December 2021 testing requirement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2021/December/new-covid-19-testing-requirement-inbound-travel), are historical. The 2023 announcement is the newest one on vaccination. I didn't find a newer ISSS post on COVID testing, so for current entry requirements, check with ISSS.

For re-entry, ISSS's [travel advisory](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2024/December/re-entry) lists these documents:
- A passport valid at least 6 months beyond your return date
- A valid F-1 or J-1 visa
- A recent travel signature on your I-20 or DS-2019
- Proof of enrollment, such as your class schedule

If you have questions about your own travel situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor.
